name: Phenylethyl resorcinol

card.summary: A skin-brightening cosmetic ingredient that inhibits tyrosinase, used in serums and eye products to fade dark spots, uneven tone and under-eye darkness.
card.note: Mostly studied in small cosmetic trials; rare contact allergy is possible with resorcinol-type ingredients.

quick.overview:
Phenylethyl resorcinol (PR), sold to formulators as Symwhite 377, is an ingredient in brightening skincare. It blocks tyrosinase, the enzyme that drives melanin production, so it is used to even skin tone and lighten dark spots or pigmented under-eye circles.

It is widely used in the personal care industry as a skin lightening ingredient, though its physicochemical properties were only fully characterised in a 2019 paper. A small randomised trial in 20 women found lower melanin index around the eyes with PR gel, especially when combined with microneedling.
quick.how: People apply products containing PR once or twice daily, typically as serums, creams or eye gels, often alongside sunscreen and other brighteners like niacinamide or vitamin C. Results in studies were assessed over weeks to a couple of months.
quick.risks: Reported side effects are generally mild. Contact allergy has been described for related resorcinol compounds such as resacetophenone in a nail product. Patch testing is a common precaution for new actives.

lead: Phenylethyl resorcinol (PR) is a synthetic resorcinol derivative used as a skin-lightening ingredient. It is marketed to cosmetic formulators as Symwhite 377 and appears in brightening serums, creams and eye products aimed at evening skin tone and lightening hyperpigmentation [1][2].

It belongs to the class of tyrosinase inhibitors, compounds that interfere with the enzyme controlling melanin synthesis [3]. Reviews of tyrosinase inhibitor design describe the target as central to pigmentation research [3].

A 2019 study noted that despite wide use, limited information existed on PR's physical properties, and reported a melting point of about 79 degrees C and a log P of 3.35, along with skin permeation data in porcine and human skin [2].

chain: More even tone and lighter dark spots or dark circles
angle.text: PR is applied to the skin to reduce melanin formation, which lightens dark spots and uneven tone. In one trial it was also used on under-eye dark circles.

paras: PR is used in cosmetic products to lighten pigmentation and even skin tone [2]. It has also been tested for infraorbital dark circles [1].

PR inhibits tyrosinase, reducing melanin production [3]. Delivery studies in porcine and human skin examined how well the molecule permeates depending on the vehicle [2]. A separate laboratory study examined cytochrome P450 3A4 metabolism of phenolic compounds [4].

Allergic contact dermatitis has been reported from the related compound resacetophenone in an antifungal nail preparation [5]. In the dark-circle trial, safety outcomes were assessed alongside efficacy [1].

A randomised controlled trial in 20 women compared PR gel with a control gel for infraorbital dark circles. Melanin index in the PR group was significantly lower than baseline at 8 weeks, with a larger drop on the side that also had nano-microneedle assistance, while the control showed no change; erythema index did not differ between sides [1].

timeline.event: Study characterises PR's physical properties and skin delivery. [2]
Randomised trial tests PR with nano-microneedles for dark circles. [1]
